keyVerseText: That no man go beyond and defraud his brother in any matter: because that the Lord is the avenger of all such, as we also have forewarned you and testified. defraud: or, oppress, or, overreach in: or, in the matter
rootMeaning: The Greek verb ὑπερβαίνω (hyperbaínō) combines ὑπέρ, meaning "over," "beyond," or "exceeding," with the base of βᾶσις, meaning "step" or "go." Literally, it conveys the idea of stepping beyond a boundary or limit. This root sense of physically going over or crossing a threshold enriches the English gloss "go beyond" by emphasizing an active surpassing or transgression of a set boundary, not merely a passive exceeding.
usageInScripture: The word ὑπερβαίνω appears only once in the New Testament, specifically in 1 Thessalonians 4:6, where it is translated as "go beyond." This single occurrence highlights a consistent semantic field of crossing limits, whether physical or moral. The fact that the top translation is "man go beyond" underscores the verb’s focus on human action in relation to boundaries, particularly ethical or relational boundaries.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ὑπερβαίνω as stepping beyond a boundary invites reflection on the holiness and moral order God establishes for His people. The verb’s root meaning underscores the seriousness of transgression, not merely as a minor slip but as an active crossing over of God-ordained limits. This enriches our grasp of sin as a deliberate overstepping that disrupts relationships, especially within the community of believers. It calls Christians to respect God’s standards and to live in obedience, trusting that God's justice will address those who overreach.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Thessalonians 4:6, the injunction that "no man go beyond and defraud his brother in any matter" uses ὑπερβαίνω to warn against overstepping ethical boundaries in relationships. The word emphasizes the act of actively crossing a line that should not be crossed, here in the form of defrauding or oppressing another believer. This highlights God’s concern for just and loving conduct among His people, reminding us that the Lord will avenge such transgressions, reinforcing the call to integrity and brotherly respect.
